messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 1734501234 - High 5xx rate detected for APAC->EU routing path. Thresholds: error_rate>4% for 5m. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/dev/alerts/1734501234

alex_oncall: I'm on it. Confirming severity, seeing ~6% 502/504s for requests routed from apac-frontends to eu-backend cluster. Latency for affected requests spiked from 120ms -> 900ms.

netops_raj: I see the same. BGP path shifts around 03:07 UTC, then our geo-steer policy started reassigning sessions. Looks like the geofence->region mapping flipped for a subset of APAC prefixes. Possible policy eval return different priority because of TTL/metric mismatch.

sre_jen: Can we pin affected prefixes to eu as a temporary mitigation? If we set pin weight to 100 for eu for those prefixes it should short-circuit the bad path while we dig in.

alex_oncall: Trying a quick policy patch now. Running the canary config against a small prefix set.

alex_oncall: (code)
PATCH /routing/policies/geo-steer HTTP/1.1
Host: controlplane.internal
Content-Type: application/json
{ "canary_prefixes": ["203.0.113.0/24","198.51.100.0/24"], "pin_target": "eu-west" }

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: regional-routing-pin -> step 2: apply canary patch, validate 5m, rollback if error_rate increases. Link: https://runbooks.redwood/regional-routing-pin

maria_oncall: Heads up I'm taking second-shift in 10. If this becomes pager escalated please handoff to me.

netops_raj: Patch applied to canary prefixes. Initial telemetry: those prefixes dropped to <0.5% errors. However, other APAC prefixes still seeing 502s.

sre_jen: Hmm, I see anomalies in DNS resolution TTLs coming from APAC resolvers — some resolvers still hold old region records with very long remaining TTLs. That would cause clients to keep hitting the misrouted edge.

support_sam: We already have two customers reporting widespread failures: AcmeCorp (APAC users) and Learnly (some EU sessions). Both report ~20% requests failing since 03:05 UTC. Logged as INC-8804 and INC-8805.

product_lee: Customer-impact note: AcmeCorp is a paid enterprise. Please add them to the incident page and notify CS. We need a customer-facing timeline and ETA for mitigation.

alex_oncall: Can we flush edge caches + nudge resolvers? Flushing global DNS is not possible, but we can lower authoritative TTL and then trigger a refresh. Lower TTL to 30s now?

netops_raj: Lowering TTL now to 30 for the affected zone. It will take time to propagate; some resolvers will ignore TTL for a while but most should pick up within 2-3 minutes. Also triggering edgestack cache purge for the misrouted prefixes.

sre_jen: Observation: when we applied the first pin patch we unintentionally introduced a fallback that assigns weight to us-east for prefixes without explicit geofence mapping. That explains Learnly seeing EU->US traffic. Rolling back that fallback should stop cross-continent spikes.

alex_oncall: Rolling back fallback now. Command: (code)
POST /routing/policies/geo-steer/rollback
{ "reason": "fallback-misassign", "rollback_to": "1723467890" }

ops-runbook-bot: Action logged. If rollback does not reduce errors in 5m, escalate to Network Eng (pager).

maria_oncall: Taking on-call now. Alex handing off: root cause suspected policy mis-eval + DNS TTL skew. Current mitigations applied: canary pin for two prefixes, TTL lowered to 30s, edgestack caches purged, fallback rolled back.

alex_oncall: Handing off to Maria. My notes: check link https://dash.redwood/dev/regions/apac-to-eu?period=15m, watch for error_rate and cross-region p50 latency, verify AcmeCorp and Learnly session logs.

maria_oncall: Acknowledged. I'll run broad pin for all affected APAC prefixes if errors persist after TTL window. Also opening a ticket with upstream CDN provider to confirm BGP stability.

netops_raj: Pushed broader pin to all APAC prefixes as temporary measure (weight=95 -> eu-west) at 03:22 UTC. Monitor: errors dropped from 6% -> 0.8% across APAC after the broader pin.

support_sam: Notifying AcmeCorp on-call and CS with a short blurb and link to the incident page. Customer wants an ETA for permanent fix.

product_lee: For the incident timeline: please record 03:05 UTC (first detection), 03:07 UTC (policy flip observed), 03:15 UTC (canary applied), 03:22 UTC (global pin applied), 03:35 UTC (errors under 1%). We will prepare a post-incident customer note.

sre_jen: Postmortem action items: 1) add pre-deploy safeguards to geo-steer policy to prevent fallback weight from exceeding threshold 2) add automated DNS TTL sanity checks on resolver telemetry 3) run a drill for TTL-heavy resolver behavior.

netops_raj: Also recommend adding a probe that validates region mapping per prefix every 1m and alerts on flip count > 2 in 5m.

maria_oncall: I'll stay on this until stabilized for 2 hours and then coordinate follow-up with infra and product. Filing follow-up ticket: INFRA-1298 (policy-hardening + probes).

support_sam: Customers updated. CS escalation opened for AcmeCorp.

incident-bot: Incident P1 created: INC-2026-1734501234. Pager notified: oncall schedule updated.

maria_oncall: Closing note: mitigation in place (global pin). Root cause likely combination: routing policy mis-eval + stale DNS entries at some APAC resolvers. We'll confirm root cause in postmortem. If anyone sees regression, ping me. :thumbsup:
